title: I wanted a stargate xcom game, so spent a couple of days chatting to Codex and.. got my stargate game :D
author: davesoft
selftext:
Hosted on the worst url in the world, my little toy game made entirely by Codex. Not perfect, and plenty of room for refinement, but it's actually fun to play, which would be impossible if I made it myself over weeks.

[https://xgate-brhrc8apfngmegar.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net/](https://xgate-brhrc8apfngmegar.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net/)

comments.author: Constant_Physics8504
comments.body: Did it make all the images? I'm actually impressed at that blocky 2.5D

replies.author: davesoft
replies.body: The dossiers were made my chatGPT in a different session, but the entire js project and all the assets were made by codex. Plenty of stuff ends up being 180 degrees in the wrong direction, but I'm impressed how creative it has been with short level descriptions and no source art. I guess it's using the internet for reference alot.

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: People need to be careful of the copyright infringements they are actively publicly posting about.

replies.author: davesoft
replies.body: There's no money in it, it's full of references to stuff.

replies.author: DocHolidayPhD
replies.body:
To ChatGPT: "Is it copyright infringement even if you do not make money on it?"  
  
Response: I’ll answer generally and flag jurisdiction differences, since copyright rules depend on where you are and what was copied.

Thought for 4s

Yes. **Not making money does not automatically prevent copyright infringement.** It can still be infringement if you copy, distribute, adapt, display, or use protected work without permission and no exception applies.

Profit matters mainly as **one factor** in defenses like U.S. fair use. Noncommercial use can help, but the U.S. Copyright Office says noncommercial use is **not automatically fair use**; fair use depends on all circumstances.

replies.author: davesoft
replies.body: I'm not afraid, but thanks for concern.
